cues.en: Hello, Internet. We need to talk about locks. The physical and the digital. In the physical world, locks aren't as good as you think they are. The lock on your door stops worries, not burglars, as two minutes of search searching will reveal. Spend more, get more, but all fail with tools and time enough.
cues.zh: 嗨，互联网。我们得聊聊锁。实体锁和数字锁。在现实世界里，锁没你想的那么可靠。你门上的锁挡住的是担忧，不是盗贼——搜两分钟就能明白。花更多钱，能买更好的锁，但只要工具够好、时间够多，全都扛不住。

cues.en: That physical locks are bad at locking mostly doesn't matter in normal life because burglars are constrained by the physical world. A burglar must cruise the neighborhood spending their time to pick a target, which makes a house that looks secure most of the way toward being secure. Each target house can then only be attacked one at a time and comes with a risk of being physically caught in the act. But digital is different. The constraints of the physical no longer apply. On the Internet, a digital lock must protect you from not just the neighborhood burglar, but all burglars everywhere. For on the Internet, there's no such thing as distance.
cues.zh: 实体锁不擅长防入侵，这在日常生活中基本无所谓，因为盗贼受现实世界约束。盗贼得在附近转悠，花时间挑目标，所以一栋看起来安全的房子，在很大程度上就已经算安全了。每个目标房子一次只能被攻击一个，而且还有被当场抓获的风险。但数字世界不一样。现实世界的约束不再适用。在互联网上，数字锁不仅要防附近的盗贼，还要防全世界所有盗贼。因为互联网上根本没有距离这回事。

cues.en: Internet burglars don't crack digital locks personally. They build burglar bots that try millions of combinations just to see what opens. One lock down the street or a country full on the other side of the world, it's all the same. Actually, other side of the world is better. A dude in East Whateverlandia stealing your identity has a near zero chance of getting caught. This is bad news, but thanks to mathematics, digital locks can be made unbreakable.
cues.zh: 网络窃贼不会亲自去破解数字锁。他们会造出窃贼机器人，尝试数百万种组合，只为了看看哪把能打开。街边的一把锁，还是地球另一端一整个国家的锁，全都一样。其实，地球另一端还更好。一个在东边某个不知名国家的家伙盗用你的身份，被抓到的概率几乎为零。这是坏消息，但多亏数学，数字锁可以被做得牢不可破。

cues.en: This is encryption,
cues.zh: 这就是加密，

cues.en: digital lock that without the password cannot be opened. Burglar bots will plow through all the possibilities, but a secure password will take longer than the heat death of the universe to guess. No password, no entry, no matter how much of a lead hacker your mom is. Your private files stay private, which might just be the greatest social good mathematics has done mankind.
cues.zh: 一种没有密码就打不开的数字锁。窃贼机器人会遍历所有可能性，但一个安全密码要猜的时间比宇宙热寂还长。没密码就进不去，不管你妈是多么顶尖的黑客。你的私人文件保持私密，这或许是数学为人类带来的最大社会福祉。

cues.en: But it's easy to imagine unbreakable
cues.zh: 但很容易想象，牢不可破的

cues.en: digital locks as bad news. Maximum lazy ticking time bomb. The location and off code of which are locked on the phone of a dead man. Now, were the information on a piece of paper in a safe room, no problem. In the physical world, if you can't crack the lock, then you crack the wall. Society agrees under this scenario, it's reasonable for police to get in no matter what it takes. Note, this means real world locks aren't just physically weak, but also legally weak. We could live in a world with privacy laws that forbade police to break into all locks no matter how flimsy, but we don't because that'd be dumb.
cues.zh: 数字锁是坏消息。一颗极其被动的定时炸弹。它的位置和关闭密码锁在一个死人的手机里。要是信息写在纸上、放在安全室里，那没问题。在物理世界里，打不开锁，就砸墙。社会认可在这种情况下，警察无论用什么手段进去都合理。注意，这意味着现实世界的锁不仅在物理上脆弱，在法律上也脆弱。我们本可以生活在一个隐私法禁止警察撬开任何锁的世界，不管锁多不结实；但我们没有，因为那太蠢了。

cues.en: This
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: is where gears turn in government heads. If digital locks are physically invulnerable,
cues.zh: 就是政府头脑里齿轮开始转动的地方。如果数字锁在物理上无懈可击，

cues.en: maybe they can be made legally vulnerable to require digital locks be built with a keyhole for which police have the key. Highly secure, top secret for emergencies only, surely. This legal
cues.zh: 也许可以让它们在法律上变得可被攻破，要求数字锁在制造时带一个警察持有钥匙的钥匙孔。当然，高度安全、绝密，仅供紧急情况使用。这种法律上的

cues.en: vulnerability
cues.zh: 脆弱性

cues.en: to ban citizens from owning perfect digital locks to require companies manufacture their devices with key holes is an idea that many, many governments are interested in. And governments point out that a warrant which lets police into your house and into papers should let police into your phone. If your home is your castle but the need pressing enough, the police bring a battering ram. But there's no battering ram to crack open a well locked phone to comply with a warrant, not helpfully anyway, which is a problem. Again, we all ideally want police to crack digital locks sometimes.
cues.zh: 就是禁止公民拥有完美的数字锁，要求公司制造带钥匙孔的设备，这是许许多多政府都感兴趣的想法。政府还指出，既然搜查令能让警察进入你的房子、翻看你的文件，那也应该能让警察进入你的手机。如果你的家是你的城堡，但只要需求足够紧迫，警察就会带来破门锤。但要遵照搜查令撬开一部锁得很好的手机，并没有破门锤可用——反正也帮不上忙，这就是问题所在。再说，理想情况下，我们都希望警察有时能破解数字锁。

cues.en: But at our current level on the tech tree, digital locks that cannot be opened are a thing that exists. And because they are made of math, something a skilled coder can build at home, trying to ban digital locks for everyone is pretty close to trying to ban an idea.
cues.zh: 以我们目前科技树上的水平，无法被打开的数字锁已经存在。而且因为它们由数学构成，熟练的程序员在家就能做出来，所以想对所有人禁止数字锁，几乎等于想禁止一种思想。

cues.en: Good luck with that. But even were it possible to successfully
cues.zh: 祝你好运。但即便有可能成功

cues.en: ban perfect digital locks in a country, remember, on the internet, there's no such thing as distance. Even if your government is a Xanadu bureaucracy of the Seraphim Incorruptible,
cues.zh: 在一个国家禁止完美的数字锁，记住，在互联网上，距离根本不存在。即便你的政府是 Xanadu 式、由不可腐蚀的炽天使组成的官僚机构，

cues.en: there are demons elsewhere. Unbreakable
cues.zh: 别处仍有恶魔。牢不可破的

cues.en: digital locks are the foundation upon which computing and internetting is built. Banking, buying, blogging, vlogging, gaming, tweeting, beating, meeting, all of this is possible because of unbreakable digital locks. They've existed since computers filled rooms, but now with computers in our pockets, we rely on those locks to protect the content of our lives, the content of our minds. Forced weakness,
cues.zh: 数字锁是计算与互联网活动赖以建立的基础。银行业务、购物、写博客、拍视频博客、玩游戏、发推、打斗、会面，这一切之所以可能，都是因为牢不可破的数字锁。从计算机还占满房间的时代起，它们就存在了；但如今计算机就在我们口袋里，我们依赖这些锁来保护我们生活的内容、我们思想的内容。强制制造的弱点，

cues.en: even with the best of intentions, places everyone
cues.zh: 即便怀着最好的意图，也会把每个人

cues.en: in danger. The nature of a keyhole is to be cracked, and the nature of the Internet is to bring demons to the door. No matter how much we might wish it, there's no way to build a digital lock that angels can open and demons cannot.
cues.zh: 置于危险之中。锁孔的本质就是被撬开，互联网的本质就是把恶魔引到门口。无论我们多么希望，都不可能造出一把天使能打开、恶魔打不开的数字锁。

cues.en: Anyone saying otherwise is either ignorant of the mathematics or less of an angel than they appear.
cues.zh: 任何否认这一点的人，要么不懂数学，要么没有看起来那么像天使。
